title: Grow the Pool, Then Spend It

scenes.tts: One pool of progenitors makes a few early neurons, then many later ones. How?
scenes.visual: Title card: Grow the Pool, Then Spend It. A pool of dots; a trickle of neurons, then a stream.
scenes.narration: One pool of progenitors makes a few early neurons, then many later ones. How?

scenes.tts: In this simple model, every division gives two daughters. Each daughter either divides again, or leaves the cycle to become a neuron.
scenes.visual: One progenitor dot splits into two daughters; one coloured stay, one coloured leave.
scenes.narration: In this simple model, every division gives two daughters. Each daughter either divides again, or leaves the cycle to become a neuron.

scenes.tts: The fraction that keeps dividing is called P. The fraction that leaves is Q, the leaving fraction. Together they make one.
scenes.visual: On screen: P + Q = 1. P labelled proliferative fraction, Q labelled leaving fraction.
scenes.narration: The fraction that keeps dividing is called P. The fraction that leaves is Q, the leaving fraction. Together they make one.

scenes.tts: The rules are on screen. The pool after a cycle depends on P. The neurons made depend on Q.
scenes.visual: Equations on screen: progenitors after = 2 × P × progenitors before; neurons made = 2 × Q × progenitors before.
scenes.narration: The rules are on screen. The pool after a cycle depends on P. The neurons made depend on Q.

scenes.tts: Walk a hundred progenitors through three cycles, with Q rising each time. Assume no cells die.
scenes.caption: Walk 100 progenitors through three cycles, with Q rising each time. Assume no cells die.
scenes.visual: 100 dots in a box. A worked table header: cycle, Q, progenitors at start, daughters, progenitors after, neurons made.
scenes.narration: Walk 100 progenitors through three cycles, with Q rising each time. Assume no cells die.

scenes.tts: When Q is point three, a hundred progenitors make sixty neurons and a hundred forty progenitors. The pool grows.
scenes.visual: Row 1: Q 0.3, 100 start, 200 daughters, 140 progenitors, 60 neurons. Pool box grows.
scenes.narration: When Q is 0.3, 100 progenitors make 60 neurons and 140 progenitors. The pool grows.
scenes.caption: When Q is 0.3, 100 progenitors make 60 neurons and 140 progenitors. The pool grows.

scenes.tts: When Q is one half, a hundred forty progenitors make a hundred forty of each. The pool holds still.
scenes.visual: Row 2: Q 0.5, 140 start, 280 daughters, 140 progenitors, 140 neurons. Pool box unchanged.
scenes.narration: When Q is 0.5, 140 progenitors make 140 of each. The pool holds still.
scenes.caption: When Q is 0.5, 140 progenitors make 140 of each. The pool holds still.

scenes.tts: When Q is point seven, they make a hundred ninety-six neurons. Only eighty-four progenitors remain, so the pool shrinks.
scenes.visual: Row 3: Q 0.7, 140 start, 280 daughters, 84 progenitors, 196 neurons. Pool box shrinks.
scenes.narration: When Q is 0.7, they make 196 neurons. Only 84 progenitors remain, so the pool shrinks.
scenes.caption: When Q is 0.7, they make 196 neurons. Only 84 progenitors remain, so the pool shrinks.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-six, Takao Takahashi, Richard Nowakowski and Verne Caviness measured Q in the mouse cortex.
scenes.caption: In 1996, Takao Takahashi, Richard Nowakowski and Verne Caviness measured Q in the mouse cortex.
scenes.visual: Credit: Takahashi, Nowakowski and Caviness, 1996, mouse dorsomedial cortex, ventricular epithelium.
scenes.narration: In 1996, Takao Takahashi, Richard Nowakowski and Verne Caviness measured Q in the mouse cortex.

scenes.tts: Q was low early. It crossed one half on embryonic day fourteen, in the eighth cycle.
scenes.caption: Q was low early. It crossed 0.5 on E14, in the eighth cycle.
scenes.visual: A Q curve over eleven cycles, E11 to E17: low early, crossing 0.5 at cycle 8 (E14).
scenes.narration: Q was low early. It crossed 0.5 on E14, in the eighth cycle.

scenes.tts: It rose to about point eight by embryonic day sixteen. Their model spanned eleven cell cycles.
scenes.caption: It rose to about 0.8 by E16. Their model spanned eleven cell cycles.
scenes.visual: The curve reaches about 0.8 at E16. Eleven cycle ticks along the axis.
scenes.narration: It rose to about 0.8 by E16. Their model spanned eleven cell cycles.

scenes.tts: The model covers the ventricular zone only. Intermediate progenitors in the subventricular zone add divisions of their own.
scenes.visual: Ventricular zone box highlighted; subventricular zone box greyed with label: extra divisions, not in the model.
scenes.narration: The model covers the ventricular zone only. Intermediate progenitors in the subventricular zone add divisions of their own.

scenes.tts: Predict. The pool stops growing in the cycle where Q reaches one half. Is that when the most neurons are made?
scenes.visual: Bar chart of pool and neurons per cycle, cycle 8 marked Q = 0.5. Predict card: is output highest here?
scenes.narration: Predict. The pool stops growing in the cycle where Q reaches one half. Is that when the most neurons are made?

scenes.tts: No. Look back at the table. The next cycle makes more neurons from the same pool.
scenes.visual: Worked table rows 2 and 3 highlighted: 140 neurons, then 196 from the same pool of 140.
scenes.narration: No. Look back at the table. The next cycle makes more neurons from the same pool.

scenes.tts: In this rising example, the pool shrinks slowly just past one half while Q climbs, so output rises one more cycle. In general, output rises only if two times one minus this Q, times the next Q, beats this Q. Later the shrinking pool wins.
scenes.visual: Two curves labelled this example: pool flattening and falling, output still rising one more cycle, then falling. On screen: output rises only if 2 × (1 − Q now) × Q next > Q now. Side note: at Q fixed at 0.5, both stay flat.
scenes.narration: In this rising example, the pool shrinks slowly just past 0.5 while Q climbs, so output rises one more cycle. In general, output rises only if 2 × (1 − this Q) × next Q beats this Q. Later the shrinking pool wins.
scenes.caption: In this rising example, the pool shrinks slowly just past 0.5 while Q climbs, so output rises one more cycle. In general, output rises only if 2 × (1 − this Q) × next Q beats this Q. Later the shrinking pool wins.

scenes.tts: In the simulation's rising sketch, output peaks in the ninth cycle, the one after Q reached one half.
scenes.caption: In the simulation's rising sketch, output peaks in the ninth cycle, the one after Q reached 0.5.
scenes.visual: Bar chart of the simulator's rising preset, Q = 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.25, 0.30, 0.35, 0.40, 0.50, 0.65, 0.80, 0.80: output tallest at cycle 9; cycle 8 marked Q = 0.5. Label: illustrative sketch, not the published fitted curve.
scenes.narration: In the simulation's rising sketch, output peaks in the ninth cycle, the one after Q reached 0.5.

scenes.tts: About seventy percent of its output comes once Q has reached one half. The exact peak depends on how Q rises.
scenes.visual: Shaded share of the eleven cycles' output from cycle 8 onward, labelled about 70 percent. Then cycle 9's Q alone is lowered to 0.6 and the peak moves to cycle 10.
scenes.narration: About 70 percent of its output comes once Q has reached 0.5. The exact peak depends on how Q rises.
scenes.caption: About 70 percent of its output comes once Q has reached 0.5. The exact peak depends on how Q rises.

scenes.tts: So the cortex first builds its pool, then spends much of it. Neurons spent later go to more superficial layers. The sketch stops at cycle eleven with progenitors left; it does not model how neurogenesis ends.
scenes.visual: Pool grows, then shrinks, with a residual pool still present at the cycle-11 cutoff; neurons leaving later are coloured upper-layer. Small note: emptying the pool in this model would need a cycle with Q = 1; real progenitors also switch to making glia.
scenes.narration: So the cortex first builds its pool, then spends much of it. Neurons spent later go to more superficial layers. The sketch stops at cycle 11 with progenitors left; it does not model how neurogenesis ends.
scenes.caption: So the cortex first builds its pool, then spends much of it. Neurons spent later go to more superficial layers. The sketch stops at cycle 11 with progenitors left; it does not model how neurogenesis ends.

scenes.tts: But the model counts how many daughters leave, not which identity they take. Do not read it as layer sizes.
scenes.visual: Label over the bars: counts, not identities; not layer sizes.
scenes.narration: But the model counts how many daughters leave, not which identity they take. Do not read it as layer sizes.

scenes.tts: Try the simulation below this film. Find the cycle with the most neurons.
scenes.visual: A preview of the lesson's interactive with the Q rising preset selected.
scenes.narration: Try the simulation below this film. Find the cycle with the most neurons.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: below one half the pool grows, and above it the pool shrinks. Output can keep rising a cycle after the pool stops growing.
scenes.caption: The takeaway: below 0.5 the pool grows, and above it the pool shrinks. Output can keep rising a cycle after the pool stops growing.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card with the Q curve and the output curve peaking one cycle after the pool.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: below 0.5 the pool grows, and above it the pool shrinks. Output can keep rising a cycle after the pool stops growing.
